daily_reality.summary: Medical dosimetrists design and calculate radiation dose distributions for cancer patients, collaborating closely with radiation oncologists and medical physicists. They work primarily at computers in hospitals or cancer treatment centers on a standard 40-hour week.
typical_tasks: Import diagnostic CT/MRI scans into treatment planning software (Eclipse, RayStation, Pinnacle)
Contour organs at risk (OARs) adjacent to tumors — spinal cord, lungs, heart, kidneys, bladder
Design and optimize IMRT, VMAT, SBRT, and SRS treatment plans
Calculate radiation dose distributions ensuring target coverage while minimizing healthy tissue exposure
Evaluate dose-volume histograms (DVHs) for plan quality assessment
Perform quality assurance (QA) testing on treatment machines
Document treatment plans comprehensively — archiving patient files and assisting with chart checks
Assist with patient simulation — positioning patients for treatment delivery
Collaborate with radiation oncologists on plan modifications and adaptations
Resolve errors in treatment delivery systems (ARIA, Mosaiq)
key_documents: Plan approval documentation from radiation oncologist

deadlines.plan_review_approval: Before first treatment fraction — same day or next business day
deadlines.qa_measurements: Monthly machine QA, daily output checks

daily_reality.seasonality: No significant seasonal variation. Cancer treatment is year-round. Slight dips around major holidays when patient starts may be deferred. Equipment upgrade/maintenance windows may create temporary workload shifts.

regulatory.summary: Medical dosimetrists are certified by the Medical Dosimetrist Certification Board (MDCB). State licensing requirements vary — some states require licensure as radiologic technicians. The field is governed by NRC regulations for radiation safety and JCAHO standards for healthcare quality.

key_regulations.name: NRC 10 CFR Part 35 — Medical Use of Byproduct Material
key_regulations.description: Federal regulations governing medical use of radioactive materials

key_regulations.name: State radiation control programs
key_regulations.description: Agreement States regulate radiation-producing machines and radioactive materials

key_regulations.name: Joint Commission (JCAHO) standards
key_regulations.description: Healthcare quality and patient safety standards

licensing_certification.primary_certification: Certified Medical Dosimetrist (CMD) — administered by MDCB
requirements: Graduation from JRCERT-accredited Medical Dosimetry program (minimum 12 months)
licensing_certification.exam_changes_2026: Beginning January 2026, candidates who fail have a 5-year period for up to 2 additional attempts. After 3rd failure, ineligible for 2 calendar years.
licensing_certification.international_route_terminated: MDCB terminated international eligibility route after September 2025 administration
licensing_certification.state_licensing: No universal state licensing specifically for dosimetrists — some states require licensure as radiologic technician or nuclear medicine technologist
licensing_certification.continuing_education: Required for CMD maintenance of certification

regulatory.penalties: Radiation safety violations can result in NRC enforcement actions, civil penalties up to $375,000 per violation per day, and potential criminal prosecution for willful violations.

tools.summary: Medical dosimetrists primarily use treatment planning systems (TPS) to design radiation therapy plans, supported by record-and-verify systems, contouring tools, and quality assurance software.

primary_software.name: Varian Eclipse
primary_software.purpose: Treatment planning system — dose calculation, plan optimization, contouring

primary_software.name: RayStation
primary_software.purpose: Treatment planning system with automated planning (ECHO algorithm in v2025), multi-criteria optimization

primary_software.name: Philips Pinnacle
primary_software.purpose: Treatment planning system — collapsed cone convolution algorithm

primary_software.name: Elekta Monaco
primary_software.purpose: Treatment planning system — Monte Carlo dose calculation

record_verify_systems.name: ARIA
record_verify_systems.purpose: Record-and-verify system for treatment delivery, patient records

ai_tools.name: Plan AI (Sun Nuclear)
ai_tools.purpose: Predicts ideal dose, auto-creates AI-guided optimization objectives via Eclipse and RayStation scripting

ai_tools.name: Auto-contouring AI
ai_tools.purpose: Delineates organs at risk — reduces contouring time from half a day to under an hour

other_tools: Patient QA software (MapCHECK, ArcCHECK, SNC Patient)
Spreadsheets for dose tracking and plan comparisons
tools.pain_points: Integration between different vendor TPS systems, learning curves for multiple platforms, software bugs during plan optimization, high cost of TPS licenses

terminology.summary: Medical dosimetry has highly technical vocabulary rooted in radiation physics, oncology, and treatment planning. Practitioners use extensive acronyms in daily communication.

key_abbreviations.IMRT: Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy — variable intensity beams for homogeneous dose distribution
key_abbreviations.VMAT: Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy — rotating cone beam with dynamic MLC, variable dose rate and gantry speed
key_abbreviations.SBRT: Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy — high-dose, few-fraction treatments
key_abbreviations.SRS: Stereotactic Radiosurgery — single-fraction high-dose cranial treatment
key_abbreviations.DVH: Dose-Volume Histogram — graphical plan quality assessment tool
key_abbreviations.OAR: Organs at Risk — healthy structures near the tumor to be spared
key_abbreviations.PTV: Planning Target Volume — includes clinical target plus margins for uncertainty
key_abbreviations.CTV: Clinical Target Volume — tumor plus microscopic disease spread
key_abbreviations.GTV: Gross Tumor Volume — visible tumor on imaging
key_abbreviations.Gy: Gray — unit of absorbed radiation dose
key_abbreviations.DICOM: Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine

common_jargon: Hot spot — area receiving higher-than-prescribed dose
Cold spot — area receiving lower-than-prescribed dose
Conform the dose — shape radiation to match tumor geometry
Inverse planning — optimizer adjusts beam parameters to meet dose constraints
Dose painting — varying dose across the target based on biological characteristics
Plan optimization — iterative process of adjusting parameters to meet dosimetric goals
Chart check — weekly verification of treatment delivery accuracy

career_psychology.summary: Medical dosimetrists are analytical healthcare professionals who work behind the scenes in radiation oncology. Career progression moves from junior dosimetrist to senior/chief dosimetrist to management or education roles.

career_levels.description: New graduates learning clinical workflows, creating basic plans under supervision
Independent plan creation for complex cases, mentoring juniors
Complex SRS/SBRT plans, protocol development, training new staff
Department management, policy creation, equipment evaluation, budgeting
Academic positions, clinical research, AAMD leadership roles

key_fears: Treatment planning errors causing patient harm
Falling behind on new technologies (AI, proton therapy)
burnout_factors: High-stakes work — errors directly affect patient outcomes
Time pressure to complete plans before treatment start dates
Expected retirement wave 2025-2030 straining remaining workforce
growth_motivation: Salary growth with experience (wide $92K range in compensation)
Transition to management, education, or vendor roles

community.summary: The AAMD (American Association of Medical Dosimetrists) is the primary professional organization, with ASTRO serving as the broader radiation oncology society. Online communities are more niche compared to larger healthcare fields.

professional_associations.name: American Association of Medical Dosimetrists (AAMD)
professional_associations.description: Primary professional organization for dosimetrists. Provides CE, advocacy, workforce surveys, and networking.
professional_associations.annual_meeting: 50th Annual Meeting: June 15-18, 2025, Caesars Palace, Las Vegas — 500+ attendees
professional_associations.member_benefits: CMD Connect online forum, regional meet-ups, 12 CE credits, Journal of Medical Dosimetry

professional_associations.name: American Society for Radiation Oncology (ASTRO)
professional_associations.description: Broader radiation oncology society — dosimetrists attend as allied health members

professional_associations.name: Medical Dosimetrist Certification Board (MDCB)
professional_associations.description: Certification body — administers CMD exam and maintenance of certification

online_communities: Reddit — no dedicated dosimetry subreddit; discussions in r/RadiationTherapy, r/RadiationOncology
conferences: AAPM Annual Meeting (medical physics, relevant to dosimetrists)

market.summary: Medical dosimetrists are a small but in-demand profession with strong salaries. The field faces a workforce shortage due to retirements, while AI is augmenting rather than replacing the role.
top_paying_states: California, New York, Massachusetts among top earners
market.annual_openings: ~200 per year (primarily replacement due to retirements and transfers)
market.workforce_shortage: AAMD projects annual shortage of 50 dosimetrists by 2035. Peak retirement rate expected between 2025-2030.
market.work_arrangements: Primarily W-2 hospital/cancer center employees. Growing remote dosimetry positions ($122K-$210K for remote roles). Some per-diem and contract positions.
market.ai_impact: AI is augmenting, not replacing dosimetrists. Auto-contouring reduces contouring time from half a day to under an hour. AI-guided optimization assists plan creation. Work has 'not decreased but shifted to more review of AI and collaboration with physicians.' Dosimetrists ranked among top 10 jobs AI will most likely augment and assist.
market_trends: Growing cancer incidence driving treatment demand
Proton therapy expansion creating specialized roles
AI integration changing workflow from creation to review/oversight
Workforce shortage due to retirement wave
